{{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Peter Welch]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Becca Balint]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Vermont}} The '''2022 United States House of Representatives election in Vermont''' was held on November 8, 2022, to elect the [[U.S. representative]] from {{ushr|VT|AL}}. The election coincided with [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]], as well as various other [[2022 United States elections|state and local elections]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Peter Welch]] was re-elected with 67.3% of the vote in [[2020 United States House of Representatives election in Vermont|2020]]. After eight-term U.S. Senator [[Patrick Leahy]] announced he would retire on November 15, some speculated that Welch might decline to seek re-election and instead seek election to the Senate.{{cite web|last=Allison|first=Natalie|title=Leahy, most senior senator, will retire|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/11/15/leahy-most-senior-senator-will-retire-522356|access-date=2021-11-16|website=POLITICO|language=en|date=November 15, 2021}} On November 22, 2021, Welch announced his candidacy for Leahy's seat, creating the first open U.S. House seat in Vermont since [[Bernie Sanders]] [[2006 United States Senate election in Vermont|ran for the U.S. Senate]] in [[2006 United States House of Representatives election in Vermont|2006]].{{cite web|last=Forgey|first=Quint|title=Rep. Peter Welch launches Senate bid for Leahy's seat|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/11/22/peter-welch-senate-campaign-patrick-leahy-seat-523176|access-date=2021-11-22|website=Politico|date=November 22, 2021}} Democratic nominee [[Becca Balint]] won the election in a landslide, becoming the first elected female member of the [[United States Congress]] in the state's history. Her main opponent in the general election, [[Liam Madden]], won the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nomination but identifies as an [[Independent politician|independent]] who opposes the [[two-party system]].{{cite news|url=https://www.wcax.com/2022/08/10/madden-face-balint-us-house-race/?outputType=amp|title=Madden 'up in the air' about accepting GOP nomination for US House|work=[[WCAX-TV]]|date=9 August 2022|access-date=14 August 2022}} Madden stated that he would not caucus with House Republicans if elected to Congress; the [[Vermont Republican Party]] later disavowed his campaign.{{Cite web |last=Cutler |first=Calvin |title=Vermont GOP will not support Liam Madden for US House |url=https://www.wcax.com/2022/08/15/vermont-gop-will-not-support-liam-madden-us-house/ |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=WCAX |date=August 15, 2022 |language=en}} Ericka Redic, who lost the Republican primary to Madden, ran in the general election as the nominee of the [[Libertarian Party of Vermont|Libertarian Party]].{{Cite web |last=Weinstein |first=Ethan |date=2022-08-11 |title=Ericka Redic, runner-up in Republican primary, running for U.S. House as a Libertarian |url=https://vtdigger.org/2022/08/11/ericka-redic-runner-up-in-republican-primary-running-for-u-s-house-as-a-libertarian/ |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=VTDigger |language=en-US}} Vermont was the last remaining state that had never elected a woman to the [[United States Congress]] after [[Mississippi]] elected its first woman, [[Cindy Hyde-Smith]], in [[2018 United States Senate special election in Mississippi|2018]]. With Balint's victory, every U.S. state has now been represented in Congress by a woman at some point. Balint is also the first openly LGBTQ person to be elected to Congress from Vermont.{{Cite web |last= |title=Becca Balint Shatters Lavender and Glass Ceilings; First LGBTQ Person and First Woman Elected to Congress from Vermont |url=https://victoryfund.org/news/becca-balint-shatters-lavender-and-glass-ceilings-first-lgbtq-person-and-first-woman-elected-to-congress-from-vermont/ |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=LGBTQ+ Victory Fund |language=en-US}} {{toclimit|2}} ==Democratic primary== [[File:MollyGrayCrop.jpg|thumb|x150px|[[Lieutenant Governor of Vermont|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Molly Gray]] finished second in the primary.]] A somewhat crowded initial primary field featuring [[President pro tempore of the Vermont Senate|Vermont Senate president pro tempore]] [[Becca Balint]], [[Vermont lieutenant governor|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Molly Gray]], state senator [[Kesha Ram Hinsdale]], former congressional staffer Sianay Chase Clifford, and physician Louis Meyers was eventually winnowed down to Balint, Gray, and Meyers following the withdrawals of Ram and Chase Clifford in mid-2022. Balint received the support of Senator [[Bernie Sanders]], and national leaders of the [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]] movement such as [[Elizabeth Warren]] and [[Pramila Jayapal]], the latter of whom backed Balint after Ram withdrew. Ram herself also supported Balint following her withdrawal.
